author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: A systematic approach to measuring organisational performance is fundamental to the pursuit of business excellence As such the area of organisational performance measurement and its use of data and analysis to inform business decisions affords statisticians a potentially high valueadding opportunity To be effective in this area statisticians need to appreciate the differing requirements for statistical information in various management zones of an enterprise This paper describes a strategy that seeks to link measurement to all facets of organisational performance particularly to desired business outcomes and also to mesh measurement with process improvement in a natural way The use of statistics and statistical thinking is then discussed in this context with particular focus on the opportunity for statisticians to have a key role at the top decisionmaking level of the organisation We argue that the role requires skills in both advanced technical statistical modelling and analysis and in statistical thinking It also requires a preparedness to form an appreciation of the business and management imperatives faced by the leaders of an enterprise and a willingness to work from this basis

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: This paper presents a comprehensive study of nonparametric measures designed to quantify angularlinear association between variables in a dataset Traditional correlation coefficients such as Pearsons r often fail to capture the complex relationships that can exist between angular and linear data We propose novel nonparametric measures that leverage rankbased methodologies to effectively identify and characterize associations without imposing parametric assumptions In particular we introduce two new statistical metrics the Angular Linear Correlation ALC and the Modified Angular Linear Distance MALD which provide robust estimations in various distributional contexts Through extensive simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate that our proposed measures outperform conventional correlation metrics especially in situations with nonlinear relationships or when outliers are present We also offer guidelines for the implementation of these measures including visualizations to aid in the interpretation of results Our findings underscore the relevance of nonparametric approaches in statistical analysis providing researchers with powerful tools for examining angularlinear associations in diverse fields such as finance meteorology and biomedical research

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: This paper presents a comprehensive review of graphical methods employed in nonparametric statistics highlighting their significance in exploratory data analysis and inference Nonparametric statistical techniques which do not assume a fixed distribution form have gained prominence due to their flexibility and robustness in various applications We systematically examine the variety of graphical tools available including box plots kernel density estimates empirical cumulative distribution functions and rankbased scatter plots Each methods utility advantages and limitations are discussed in detail with emphasis on their application in visualizing data patterns assessing assumptions and enhancing the interpretability of nonparametric analyses Additionally we provide an annotated bibliography that compiles influential works in the field categorizing them by graphical methods and their applications This bibliography serves as a resource for researchers seeking to deepen their understanding of nonparametric techniques and the role of graphical representations in statistical inference Through this review we aim to bridge the gap between theoretical developments and practical applications of graphical methods in nonparametric statistics thereby encouraging further exploration and innovation in this vital area of statistical research

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In today s datadriven environment the ability to harness statistical methods and foster statistical thinking has become paramount for enhancing organizational performance This paper explores the intersection of statistics and organizational theory presenting a framework where statistical techniques can be systematically integrated into decisionmaking processes We begin by defining statistical thinking an approach that emphasizes the importance of data variability and the context in which decisions are made Through empirical studies and case analyses across various industries we showcase how organizations that embrace statistical methodologies experience significant improvements in operational efficiency strategic planning and overall performance Additionally we identify key barriers to the adoption of statistical thinking and propose actionable strategies for cultivating a datacentric culture Our findings highlight the transformative potential of applying statistical principles not just as analytical tools but as a fundamental component of organizational mindset ultimately leading to sustainable growth and competitive advantage This paper aims to provide practitioners and leaders with insights and practical guidelines for leveraging statistics in the pursuit of excellence in organizational performance

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: This paper presents a comprehensive dialogue with Jef Teugels a prominent figure in the field of statistics renowned for his contributions to the theory of statistical inference and the development of probabilistic models Through a series of thoughtprovoking questions and responses we explore Teugels insights on the evolution of statistical methodologies the importance of robust statistical practices and the integration of modern computational tools in statistical analysis The conversation delves into contemporary challenges faced by statisticians including issues of data ethics reproducibility and the role of statistical literacy in various disciplines By reflecting on Teugels experiences and perspectives this paper aims to illuminate the enduring relevance of statistical principles in an increasingly datadriven world while also highlighting pathways for future research and education in the field The dialogue serves not only as a tribute to Teugels legacy but also as a resource for emerging statisticians and researchers seeking to navigate the complexities of modern statistical practice

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In the realm of spatial analysis understanding the relationship between spatially distributed events and associated covariates is crucial for effective modeling and prediction This paper investigates the integration of spatial logistic regression methodologies with the changeofsupport problem inherent in Poisson point processes We develop a robust framework that allows for the estimation of spatial logit models under varying spatial supports addressing challenges related to the scale of observation and data aggregation By leveraging techniques from both geostatistics and point process theory we derive conditions under which the estimates remain consistent and asymptotically normal despite changes in support Our approach is further validated through simulations and application to realworld datasets in ecology and urban studies The results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in providing accurate predictions and insights into the spatial dynamics of events paving the way for improved decisionmaking in spatiallyinformed applications Through this work we contribute to the statistical literature by bridging the gap between logistic regression models and Poisson point process frameworks offering a novel perspective on spatial data analysis

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In problems of medical imaging and robotic vision measurements of a convex set are sometimes obtained via the sets support function The standard way in which the convex set is recovered from such data is to suppose that it is polygonal model the errors as Normal random variables and apply constrained maximum likelihood methods Typically the number of sides assumed of the polygon is equal to or a little less than the number of data points However from a statistical viewpoint the number of sides should really be interpreted as a smoothing parameter and chosen to optimize some measure of performance Additionally if the true set is not a polygon then a polygonal estimate can be aesthetically unsatisfactory In this article we suggest periodic smoothing methods for estimating the convex set

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In Geographical Information Systems spatial point pattern data are often analysed by dividing space into pixels recording the presence or absence of points in each pixel and fitting alogistic regression We study weaknesses of this approach propose improvements and demonstrate an application to prospective geology in Western Australia Models based on different pixel grids are incompatible a changeofsupport problem unless the pixels are very small On a fine pixel grid a spatial logistic regression is approximately a Poisson point process with log linear intensity we give explicit distributional bounds For a loglinear Poisson process the optimal parameter estimator from pixel data is not spatial logistic regression but complementary loglog regression with an offset depending on pixel area If the pixel raster is randomly sub sampled logistic regression is conditionally optimal Bias and efficiency depend strongly on the spatial regularity of the covariates For discontinuous covariates we propose a new algorithmic strategy in which pixels are subdivided and demonstrate its efficiency

text: General models of association between an angular and a linear variable corresponding to monotone association between two linear variables are proposed Ustatistics which are analogues of Kendalls tau are developed to measure such association their distributions obtained and their performances compared with other measures of angularlinear association

text: AbstractIn this paper we present an engaging dialogue with Jerry Friedman a prominent figure in the field of statistics renowned for his contributions to statistical methodology and its applications Through a series of structured interviews we explore Friedmans insights on the evolution of statistical practices the intersection of theory and application and the future directions of the discipline Key themes include the role of computational advancements in statistical modeling the significance of reproducibility in research and the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration in addressing complex datadriven challenges By weaving together qualitative reflections and quantitative insights we aim to provide a nuanced understanding of Friedmans impact on statistical science and foster a dialogue among practitioners and scholars on the continuing evolution of the field This conversation not only highlights Friedmans personal journey but also serves as a catalyst for future discussions on the pivotal role of statistics in an increasingly datacentric world

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In this paper we investigate the problem of estimating a convex set from noisy observations of its support function The support function defined as the maximum inner product between a fixed direction and points on the boundary of a convex set provides a powerful tool for characterizing convex geometries Our approach addresses the challenges posed by noise in the data which is a common issue in practical applications We propose a novel estimation algorithm that leverages regularization techniques to enhance robustness to noise and to ensure the convexity of the estimated set Through theoretical analysis we establish convergence rates for our estimator demonstrating that under certain conditions our method is consistent and asymptotically efficient Furthermore we provide numerical simulations to illustrate the performance of our algorithm compared to existing techniques highlighting its advantages in terms of accuracy and reliability in reconstructing convex shapes from noisy support function data Our results contribute to the fields of convex analysis and statistical shape estimation offering a framework for applications in areas such as computer vision machine learning and shape recovery from empirical data

text: The problem of identifying the number of modal groups manifested in a sample of data is of continuing interest and importance in statistical practice In this paper we combine features of two current approaches to the modetesting problem with some new ideas to produce a method that provides the data analyst with a powerful and flexible way of exploring modality in univariate data This approach also provides what appears to be the first satisfactory test of modality for samples of circular data

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: Methods are proposed for constructing bootstrap confidence regions for the mean direction of a random pdimensional unit vector X with an arbitrary unimodal distribution on the p sphere The approach of this article differs from that of other authors in that it is based on pivotal statistics A general pivotal method is introduced that produces a wide variety of confidence regions on general pdimensional spheres included are confidence cones and likelihoodbased regions It can readily be modified to incorporate extra assumptions about the underlying distribution such as rotational symmetry The general method leads to confidence pictures which present information about the estimated posterior likelihood of mean orientation by shading spherical surfaces An application is given to a sample of spherical crossbed measurements The methods extend to the case where X has random length and to calculation of confidence regions for reference directions of axial bipolar or girdle distributions

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In this paper we introduce a novel approach to the computation and application of spherical medians in highdimensional data analysis The spherical median serves as a robust central tendency measure for data points represented on the surface of a unit sphere effectively addressing the challenges posed by circular and spherical geometries We begin by defining the spherical median as the point that minimizes the sum of distances to the data points utilizing a comprehensive statistical framework that incorporates both geodesic distances and the inherent properties of spherical coordinates We propose an efficient algorithm for estimating the spherical median including a convergence analysis that guarantees robustness against outliers and nonuniform data distributions Through extensive simulations and realworld applications we demonstrate the methodological advantages of spherical medians compared to traditional central tendency measures particularly in diverse fields such as directional statistics geospatial analysis and image processing The results highlight the efficacy of spherical medians in accurately capturing the central structure of spherical data sets thereby providing a valuable statistical tool for researchers and practitioners

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the asymptotic properties of multimodality tests that rely on kernel density estimates Multimodality the presence of multiple local maxima in a distribution is an important characteristic in various fields such as finance biology and machine learning Our study provides a comprehensive analysis of the statistical behavior of these tests as sample sizes approach infinity We derive the asymptotic distributions of the test statistics under both null and alternative hypotheses revealing the conditions under which the tests maintain consistency and exhibit statistical power We also examine the impact of bandwidth selection on the performance of the kernel density estimates and propose optimal bandwidth choices to enhance the robustness of the multimodality tests Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate the practical applicability of our theoretical results and compare the performance of various multimodality tests using kernel density techniques Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of multimodality detection and provide valuable insights into the design of efficient statistical tests in multimodal contexts

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In an era where datadriven decisionmaking is paramount the role of statisticians in business and industry warrants critical examination This paper explores the Industrial Statistics Divide a conceptual gap between traditional statistical methodologies and the evolving needs of modern businesses Through a comprehensive analysis of industry case studies survey data from practitioners and a review of current statistical practices we assess the relevance of statisticians in guiding strategic decisions We investigate prevalent barriers to collaboration including misconceptions about statistical methods and the increasing reliance on automated data analytics and machine learning algorithms Our findings reveal that while the demand for statistical expertise remains high an urgent need exists for statisticians to adapt their skills integrate with crossdisciplinary teams and communicate effectively in business contexts We propose actionable strategies for closing this divide ultimately enhancing the utility of statistical disciplines in driving actionable insights and fostering innovation in a competitive landscape This paper contributes to the discourse on statisticians roles in industry advocating for a paradigm shift that aligns statistical education and practice with the practical realities of modern business environments

text: AbstractIn this paper we introduce a novel approach for mode testing in statistical distributions using the Excess Mass Estimate EME Traditional methods for mode testing often rely on parametric assumptions or nonparametric techniques that can be sensitive to sample size and underlying data distribution The EME a flexible nonparametric tool measures the concentration of mass in the vicinity of a mode providing a robust framework for assessing the presence and significance of modes in a dataset We derive new asymptotic properties for the EME under various conditions and develop a hypothesis testing framework based on these properties Simulation studies illustrate the performance of our mode testing procedure compared to established methods highlighting its advantages in terms of power and robustness particularly in multimodal scenarios and in the presence of noise Additionally we apply our method to several realworld datasets demonstrating its practical utility in fields such as ecology finance and sociology where understanding modal structures is crucial Our findings suggest that the Excess Mass Estimate not only serves as a reliable measure for mode detection but also enriches the statistical toolkit for practitioners facing complex data landscapes

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In directional statistics the analysis of data that wraps around a circle such as angles and orientations presents unique challenges particularly when estimating confidence regions This paper introduces a novel approach to constructing bootstrap confidence regions for directional data utilizing both parametric and nonparametric methods We begin by reviewing existing methodologies in directional confidence region estimation highlighting their limitations We then develop a robust bootstrap algorithm tailored for circular data which incorporates resampling techniques that preserve the inherent circular structure of the data Through extensive simulations we evaluate the performance of our proposed method against traditional confidence region techniques examining criteria such as coverage probability and width Our findings demonstrate that the bootstrap confidence regions maintain higher accuracy and offer better coverage properties particularly in scenarios involving small sample sizes or skewed distributions We apply our method to realworld directional datasets illustrating its practical efficacy and potential for broader applications in fields such as meteorology biology and geophysics This work contributes to the statistical tools available for analyzing directional data reinforcing the importance of tailored methodologies for complex data types

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: Much of the practical interest attached to curves and surfaces derives from features of roughness rather than smoothness For example considerable attention has been paid to fractal models of curves and surfaces for which the notions of a normal and curvature are usually not well defined Nevertheless these quantities are sometimes measurable because the device for recording a rough surface such as a stylus or compass adds its own intrinsic smoothness In this paper we address the effect of such smoothing operations on the multivariate statistical properties of a normal to the surface Particular attention is paid to the validity of commonly assumed unimodal approximations to the distribution of the normal It is shown that the actual distribution may have more than one mode although in a range of situations the unimodal approximation is valid C Academic Press Inc

text: In this paper we investigate the effects of smoothing techniques on the multivariate statistical properties of the normal vector to a rough curve or surface As data collection methods increasingly yield highdimensional datasets characterized by inherent variability and noise understanding the influence of smoothing is critical for accurate statistical analysis and interpretation We employ several smoothing algorithms including kernel smoothing moving averages and spline fitting to assess their impact on the mean variance and covariance structure of the normals to both synthetic and realworld rough surfaces Through extensive simulations and empirical examinations we demonstrate that smoothing can significantly alter the statistical properties of normals introducing biases that may affect downstream analyses such as manifold learning and principal component analysis Our findings provide valuable insights into the tradeoffs between noise reduction and the preservation of the underlying geometric structure highlighting the necessity of careful selection and validation of smoothing techniques in multivariate statistical methodology These results contribute to a deeper understanding of the complexities involved in modeling and analyzing rough geometrical objects and inform best practices in applied statistical research

text: In this paper we address the challenge of estimating the common mean direction of several circular or spherical distributions that exhibit varying degrees of dispersion Such scenarios frequently arise in fields such as biology meteorology and directional statistics where the focus is often on understanding the central tendency of phenomena distributed in a circular or spherical space while accounting for their inherent variability We propose a novel statistical method that combines the principles of angular statistics with robust estimation techniques Our approach employs an optimization framework to identify the mean direction that minimizes a weighted error function thereby accommodating the differing dispersions of the input distributions We establish the asymptotic properties of our estimator including consistency and asymptotic normality and provide a computational algorithm for practical implementation Simulations demonstrate the efficacy of our method in various scenarios outperforming traditional estimators that do not account for dispersion differences Finally we illustrate our methodology through a realworld application highlighting its utility in accurately assessing the common mean direction in ecological data where group behaviors exhibit varying levels of dispersion This work advances the understanding of directional data analysis and offers valuable tools for researchers and practitioners dealing with multisource directional information

text: In the field of survey research obtaining accurate responses is critical for data integrity and the validity of conclusions drawn from analysis However survey responses often suffer from various forms of bias and incomplete data which can skew results This paper presents a straightforward application of the ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm to address issues related to missing data and measurement error in survey responses We outline the theoretical foundation of the EM algorithm and detail its implementation in the context of survey data analysis Our approach involves iteratively estimating the parameters of interest and the missing data leading to improved estimates of survey responses that better reflect the true underlying phenomena We showcase the efficacy of our method through a series of simulations and realworld applications demonstrating how the EM algorithm can significantly enhance the reliability of surveybased conclusions The findings suggest that the application of the EM algorithm not only yields more accurate results but also provides a robust framework for dealing with complexities inherent in survey data This research contributes to the body of knowledge on survey methodology and statistical inference offering practitioners a valuable tool for refining their analyses and improving the quality of insights drawn from survey data

text: We describe algorithms for exact computation of nonparametric bootstrap estimators and show that they are practicable for small samples It is argued that in this setting enumeration and calculation of the entire bootstrap distribution is competitive with simulation For example if the sample size is n then the entire bootstrap distribution has only atoms and exact calculation is competitive with simulation involving several hundred replications We also describe the role of exact computation in the iterated bootstrap and discuss a method of importance resampling appropriate to small samples

text: This paper considers the problem of regressing an angular response variate on a set of linear explanatory variables A general class of models is proposed in which the mean direction and dispersion of a von Mises variate are related to the explanatory variables by general link functions Appropriate regression diagnostics estimation and testing procedures are developed for fitting the models The meaning of correlation between an angular and a linear variable is clarified and leads to a general notion of multiple correlation associated with the regression model The methods are applied to a set of data arising from a study of movements of intertidal gastropods

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: This paper explores the properties and applications of spherical splines a generalization of traditional spline functions adapted for spherical domains Spherical splines offer a robust framework for interpolating and smoothing data on the surface of a sphere which is pertinent in a variety of fields including geophysics computer graphics and environmental modeling We provide a comprehensive review of the theoretical foundations of spherical splines emphasizing their unique advantages in handling boundary conditions and maintaining smoothness over spherical geometry Additionally we introduce novel computational methods for efficiently implementing spherical splines enabling their application to large datasets Through illustrative examples and computational experiments we demonstrate the effectiveness of spherical splines in reconstructing complex surface phenomena and fitting data collected from spherical domains Our findings highlight the potential of spherical splines as a powerful tool in statistical modeling and data analysis on spherical surfaces paving the way for future research and applications in this emerging area

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In this paper we introduce and evaluate a set of regression models specifically designed for analyzing angular response data which frequently manifests in fields such as directional statistics ecology and neurosciences Traditional linear regression techniques often falter in the presence of angular data due to its circular nature resulting in biased estimates and flawed inferences We propose a framework that incorporates both circular linear regression and generalized linear models tailored to angular responses facilitating accurate modeling of such data By leveraging techniques like the von Mises distribution and circular regression coefficients our models effectively account for the periodicity of angular measurements We illustrate the application of these models through simulations and realworld datasets comparing their performance with conventional regression approaches Our findings highlight the advantages of using specialized regression models for angular response demonstrating improved parameter estimation and prediction accuracy This work contributes to the methodology of statistical analysis involving angular data offering researchers a robust toolset for deriving insights from their observations

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In the realm of statistical inference the challenge of drawing reliable conclusions from small sample sizes is a welldocumented issue This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into the application of bootstrap algorithms as a method for enhancing statistical estimation and hypothesis testing when data is limited We critically evaluate various bootstrap techniques including the basic bootstrap paired bootstrap and wild bootstrap analyzing their efficacy across different statistical models and scenarios Our results indicate that bootstrap methods significantly improve the robustness of parameter estimates confidence intervals and pvalues compared to traditional methods under small sample conditions Additionally we conduct extensive simulations to assess the performance of these algorithms in terms of bias variance and coverage probability The findings underscore the value of bootstrap methodologies in mitigating the inherent instability associated with small sample sizes We also provide practical guidance on implementing bootstrap techniques in realworld applications facilitating improved decisionmaking across diverse fields such as medicine social sciences and economics Ultimately this study enhances the understanding of bootstrap algorithms and their critical role in advancing statistical practice where data is scarce

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In the realm of highdimensional data analysis identifying and characterizing significant structures or bumps is crucial for understanding complex phenomena This paper introduces a novel methodology for detecting and analyzing bumps in highdimensional datasets leveraging a combination of statistical modeling dimensionality reduction techniques and machine learning algorithms We propose a robust framework that integrates kernel density estimation with adaptive clustering methods allowing us to effectively visualize and interpret the local maxima within highdimensional spaces Our approach addresses challenges such as curse of dimensionality and overfitting providing a systematic pathway for uncovering meaningful patterns in data We validate our methodology through a series of simulations and realworld applications across diverse fields including genomics finance and social sciences The results demonstrate significant improvements in bump detection accuracy compared to existing methods underscoring the potential of our framework for advancing highdimensional data exploration This work contributes to the growing body of literature on highdimensional data analysis and opens new avenues for future research on unsupervised learning and structure detection in complex datasets

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In the field of survey research obtaining accurate responses is critical for data integrity and the validity of conclusions drawn from analysis However survey responses often suffer from various forms of bias and incomplete data which can skew results This paper presents a straightforward application of the ExpectationMaximization EM algorithm to address issues related to missing data and measurement error in survey responses We outline the theoretical foundation of the EM algorithm and detail its implementation in the context of survey data analysis Our approach involves iteratively estimating the parameters of interest and the missing data leading to improved estimates of survey responses that better reflect the true underlying phenomena We showcase the efficacy of our method through a series of simulations and realworld applications demonstrating how the EM algorithm can significantly enhance the reliability of surveybased conclusions The findings suggest that the application of the EM algorithm not only yields more accurate results but also provides a robust framework for dealing with complexities inherent in survey data This research contributes to the body of knowledge on survey methodology and statistical inference offering practitioners a valuable tool for refining their analyses and improving the quality of insights drawn from survey data

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the asymptotic properties of multimodality tests that rely on kernel density estimates Multimodality the presence of multiple local maxima in a distribution is an important characteristic in various fields such as finance biology and machine learning Our study provides a comprehensive analysis of the statistical behavior of these tests as sample sizes approach infinity We derive the asymptotic distributions of the test statistics under both null and alternative hypotheses revealing the conditions under which the tests maintain consistency and exhibit statistical power We also examine the impact of bandwidth selection on the performance of the kernel density estimates and propose optimal bandwidth choices to enhance the robustness of the multimodality tests Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate the practical applicability of our theoretical results and compare the performance of various multimodality tests using kernel density techniques Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of multimodality detection and provide valuable insights into the design of efficient statistical tests in multimodal contexts

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: A test due to BW Silverman for modality of a probability density is based on counting modes of a kernel density estimator and the idea of critical smoothing An asymptotic formula is given for the expected number of modes This together with other methods establishes the rate of convergence of the critically smoothed bandwidth These ideas are extended to provide insight concerning the behaviour of the test based on bootstrap critical values

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: Many data analytic questions can be formulated as noisy optimization problems They explicitly or implicitly involve finding simultaneous combinations of values for a set of input variables that imply unusually large or small values of another designated output variable Specifically one seeks a set of subregions of the input variable space within which the value of the output variable is considerably larger or smaller than its average value over the entire input domain In addition it is usually desired that these regions be describable in an interpretable form involving simple statements rules concerning the input values This paper presents a procedure directed towards this goal based on the notion of patient rule induction This patient strategy is contrasted with the greedy ones used by most rule induction methods and semigreedy ones used by some partitioning tree techniques such as CART Applications involving scientific and commercial data bases are presented

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: This paper presents a comprehensive study of nonparametric measures designed to quantify angularlinear association between variables in a dataset Traditional correlation coefficients such as Pearsons r often fail to capture the complex relationships that can exist between angular and linear data We propose novel nonparametric measures that leverage rankbased methodologies to effectively identify and characterize associations without imposing parametric assumptions In particular we introduce two new statistical metrics the Angular Linear Correlation ALC and the Modified Angular Linear Distance MALD which provide robust estimations in various distributional contexts Through extensive simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate that our proposed measures outperform conventional correlation metrics especially in situations with nonlinear relationships or when outliers are present We also offer guidelines for the implementation of these measures including visualizations to aid in the interpretation of results Our findings underscore the relevance of nonparametric approaches in statistical analysis providing researchers with powerful tools for examining angularlinear associations in diverse fields such as finance meteorology and biomedical research

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: This paper is concerned with the theory of unbiased estimation for nonparametric families of distributions subject to generalised moment restrictions Necessary and sufficient conditions under which symmetric statistics are unique minimum variance unbiased estimators of their expectations are obtained and some new boundedly complete families of distributions are exhibited

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: This paper commemorates the contributions of Wassily Hoeffding a pioneering statistician whose work has profoundly influenced the fields of probability theory and statistical inference We highlight Hoeffdings pivotal contributions including his formulation of the Hoeffding inequality which offers critical bounds on the sum of random variables and has become a cornerstone in both theoretical and applied statistics Through a retrospective analysis we assess the impact of his work on contemporary statistical methodologies including advancements in nonparametric statistics and the foundations of modern machine learning We also explore Hoeffdings innovative approaches to the law of large numbers and the central limit theorem underscoring how his insights continue to shape research paradigms By examining the historical context and relevance of Hoeffdings work this paper aims to inspire future generations of statisticians to build upon his legacy fostering a deeper understanding of the principles underlying statistical inference and their application in solving realworld problems

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: Spherical analogues of the linear and spatial medians are proposed for unimodal bipolar axial and girdle distributions on the sphere For unimodal data the statistical properties of the sample spherical median direction are studied including comparison with the sample mean direction in the case of Fishers distribution Spherical analogues of the one and ksample sign test are suggested The paper parallels the discussion by Brown for the spatial median

text: O wad some Power the giftie gie us To see oursels as ithers see us It wad frae mony a blunder free us An foolish notion Robert Burns To a Louse The stated purpose of this conference contains the provocative assertion that does not receive the recognition it needs as a vital part of making progress in business and industry I agree I believe that there is a significant divide between senior management in business and industry Them and the statisticians Us who work on business and industrial problems in a sense to borrow from George Bernard Shawtwo groups divided by lack of a common language A lot of their words arent in our vocabulary and a lot of our words arent in theirs Such is not the case in many other major domains of statistical practiceGovernment Insurance Medicine to name but three Why is this so and what can we do about it in Business and Industry This paper seeks to explore these questions and to argue that their resolution will involve a sustained commitment by the Statistics profession to areas such as statistical education public awareness and promoting professionalism in the practice of Statistics However the most important commitment might need to be that the Statistics profession take Robert Burns to heart

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In an era where datadriven decisionmaking is paramount the role of statisticians in business and industry warrants critical examination This paper explores the Industrial Statistics Divide a conceptual gap between traditional statistical methodologies and the evolving needs of modern businesses Through a comprehensive analysis of industry case studies survey data from practitioners and a review of current statistical practices we assess the relevance of statisticians in guiding strategic decisions We investigate prevalent barriers to collaboration including misconceptions about statistical methods and the increasing reliance on automated data analytics and machine learning algorithms Our findings reveal that while the demand for statistical expertise remains high an urgent need exists for statisticians to adapt their skills integrate with crossdisciplinary teams and communicate effectively in business contexts We propose actionable strategies for closing this divide ultimately enhancing the utility of statistical disciplines in driving actionable insights and fostering innovation in a competitive landscape This paper contributes to the discourse on statisticians roles in industry advocating for a paradigm shift that aligns statistical education and practice with the practical realities of modern business environments

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In this paper we explore unbiased estimation techniques for a class of nonparametric families of probability distributions Nonparametric models have gained increasing prominence in statistical inference due to their flexibility and ability to adapt to data without imposing strict parametric assumptions We focus on developing unbiased estimators for various distributional characteristics including location scale and higher moments within specific nonparametric frameworks By utilizing a combination of kernel density estimation and empirical distribution functions we derive conditions under which our estimators retain their unbiasedness across a range of sample sizes and distribution types We also conduct a comparative analysis with traditional parametric methods demonstrating the benefits and limitations of nonparametric estimation in scenarios where data may violate standard parametric assumptions Through extensive simulations and realdata applications we validate the theoretical findings and provide practical recommendations for statisticians employing nonparametric techniques in their analyses The outcomes of this study contribute to a deeper understanding of unbiased estimation in nonparametric settings paving the way for future research in this crucial area of statistical methodology

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: General models of association between an angular and a linear variable corresponding to monotone association between two linear variables are proposed Ustatistics which are analogues of Kendalls tau are developed to measure such association their distributions obtained and their performances compared with other measures of angularlinear association

text: This paper presents two families of curves for interpolating and smoothing sequences of points on the surface of the unit sphere One family is a natural analogue of the usual splines for curvefitting in the plane the other is slightly less optimal but more convenient from a computational viewpoint

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: In this paper we introduce a novel approach to the computation and application of spherical medians in highdimensional data analysis The spherical median serves as a robust central tendency measure for data points represented on the surface of a unit sphere effectively addressing the challenges posed by circular and spherical geometries We begin by defining the spherical median as the point that minimizes the sum of distances to the data points utilizing a comprehensive statistical framework that incorporates both geodesic distances and the inherent properties of spherical coordinates We propose an efficient algorithm for estimating the spherical median including a convergence analysis that guarantees robustness against outliers and nonuniform data distributions Through extensive simulations and realworld applications we demonstrate the methodological advantages of spherical medians compared to traditional central tendency measures particularly in diverse fields such as directional statistics geospatial analysis and image processing The results highlight the efficacy of spherical medians in accurately capturing the central structure of spherical data sets thereby providing a valuable statistical tool for researchers and practitioners

author: Nicholas I. Fisher
text: Wasssily Hoeffdings terminal illness and untimely death in put an end to efforts that were made to interview him for Statistical Science An account of his scientific work is given in Fisher and Sen but the present authors felt that the statistical community should also be told about the life of this remarkable man He contributed much to statistical science but will also live on in the memory of those who knew him as a kind and modest teacher and friend whose courage and learning were matched by a wonderful sense of humor
